svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Signalling chemicals are chemically diverse."], [1, "Amines, peptides and proteins, steroids, and others such as amino acids and a gas."], [6, "Their chemistry decides what they can do: peptides stay outside the cell..."], [8.5, "...steroids slip through the membrane, and nitric oxide diffuses fast."], [12, "Diversity lets each signal be specific to its own receptors."]]
svg.title: The chemical diversity of signals
svg.desc: Four groups of signalling chemicals, amines, peptides and proteins, steroids, and others including amino acids, acetylcholine and nitric oxide, with how their chemistry affects whether they cross the plasma membrane.

g.data-info: Made from a single amino acid. Hormones: adrenaline, thyroxine. Neurotransmitters: dopamine, serotonin, noradrenaline.
Chains of amino acids. Hormones: insulin, ADH, FSH. Neurotransmitters: endorphins.
Made from cholesterol: four fused carbon rings. Hormones: oestradiol, testosterone, cortisol.
Amino acids (glutamate, GABA), acetylcholine, and even a gas: nitric oxide (NO).
Hydrophilic peptides and amines stay outside and bind surface receptors; hydrophobic steroids pass through the membrane; small molecules such as NO diffuse quickly.

g.text: peptide: hydrophilic, binds a surface receptor

g.data-info: Each signal can be specific to its own receptors and targets without interfering with the others.

g.text: diversity → each signal specific to its own receptors and targets
